items.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
items.one_liner: Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME) matches or beats test-time training performance on scientific tasks while slashing computational costs by over 80%.
items.summary: While test-time training (TTT) enables open-weight LLMs to excel at scientific discovery, online weight updates introduce substantial computational overhead. To address this, researchers introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method that continually updates external memory without altering model weights. Evaluated across five mathematical discovery tasks, TTME outperforms TTT while drastically cutting computational costs. Specifically, TTME reduces FLOPs by 82.8% to 84.6% and runtime by 47.7% to 58.4%. These findings position memory evolution as a highly efficient alternative to weight updates for scientific tasks.
items.bottom_line: Updating external memory at test-time can replace costly model weight updates for LLM-driven scientific discovery while saving substantial compute.
